context: A uni student interviews a retired editor about literary trends
purpose: Teach: 風土/風潮/全集/もたらさ/変形/楽譜/かかわっ/遂に

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 今日はお時間ありがとうございます。卒論で戦後文学の風潮について調べていまして。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. I'm researching postwar literary trends for my thesis.
lines.style: Polite university student opening, slightly nervous but professional academic tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いやぁ、もう引退した身でね。長く編集にかかわってきたから、話せることはあるよ。
lines.en: Well, I'm retired now, but I was involved in editing for a long time, so I can share something.
lines.style: Elderly retired editor, warm reflective voice with gentle modesty.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 戦後の文壇には独特の風土があったと聞きます。何によって、それがもたらされたのでしょうか。
lines.en: I've heard the postwar literary world had a unique culture. By what was that brought about?
lines.style: Curious student asking a thoughtful, well-prepared question with measured delivery.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 焼け跡からの再出発さ。紙も乏しい中で、作家たちは遂に新しい表現にたどり着いたんだ。
lines.en: It was a restart from the ruins. With paper so scarce, writers finally arrived at new forms of expression.
lines.style: Nostalgic elder recalling hardship, measured pace with quiet emphasis.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: その時代の全集を図書館で読みましたが、戦前の文体が大きく変形していく様子が興味深かったです。
lines.en: I read the complete works of that era at the library; how the prewar style was reshaped was fascinating.
lines.style: Engaged student showing academic enthusiasm and genuine curiosity in tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうそう。詩なんかも、楽譜みたいにリズムを刻む作品が増えてね。
lines.en: Exactly. Even poetry, you saw more works that beat out rhythms like a musical score.
lines.style: Animated elder warming to the topic, hands gesturing in conversation.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。当時の編集者として、特に印象に残っている作家はいらっしゃいますか。
lines.en: I see. As an editor back then, was there a writer who left a particularly strong impression?
lines.style: Respectful follow-up question, leaning forward with active interest.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 一人いたよ。原稿を真っ赤に直しても、次の版でみんなを唸らせる男がいてね。
lines.en: There was one. Even after heavy red-ink edits, he'd bring back a draft that made everyone groan in admiration.
lines.style: Fond reminiscing elder, voice softening with respect for an old colleague.
